fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` converts CloudWatch token counts
into dollars via a rate table derived daily from Cost Explorer and matched to
models by string heuristics. That layer produced four defects in the twelve days
since the cap was deployed (2026-09-12):

1. `_rate_for`/`_match` direction-suffix collision: candidate suffix
   `input-token-count` also matches `...-cache-write-input-token-count` and the
   longest match wins, so a model's input rate resolves to its cache-write rate.
   Fires iff the ModelId has no version suffix — live for `claude-sonnet-4-6`,
   `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-5`.
2. `_normalise` mismatch: label `Nova2.0Lite` gives `nova20lite`, model id
   `us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0` gives `nova2litev10`. Neither contains the other,
   so a correct rate already in the table is missed and the model falls to
   `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`, set far above any real rate.
3. `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, the hardcoded CE service allowlist introduced by
   3083-ada3-3a0f-4051, omits `Claude Opus 4.8`, `Claude Opus 5`, `Claude Opus
   4.5`, `Cohere Rerank v3.5` and `Claude 3 Haiku`, so the authoritative CE
   signal sees about a third of real Bedrock spend.
4. `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` handles only CamelCase usage types. AWS bills
   newer marketplace models in snake_case (`USE1_input_tokens_standard-Units`)
   and publishes `_Global` variants; `_refresh_rates` skips both silently.

Two reached production unalarmed: one model priced at the fail-closed fallback
rate for seven days, emitting 6,112 `fail-closed fallback` log events while the
estimate ran at roughly twice settled billing; and the marketplace-units defect
fixed by Gerrit 3032, where the estimate was five orders of magnitude high.

These are one class, not four bugs: matching model identifiers against billing
labels with substring and suffix heuristics. Four shapes have already occurred.

## Approach

Delete the pricing-derivation layer; price every token at a ceiling rate for its
direction, set above the highest per-direction rate observed on this account, so
the estimate is an upper bound and the cap cannot fire late. Per UTC day:

    spend = max( sum over regions and the four token metrics of
                   undimensioned CloudWatch Sum * CEILING[metric],
                 ce_spend )

Cost Explorer stays in the enforcement expression: it is the only signal covering
Bedrock spend that publishes no token metric (Cohere Rerank is live; provisioned
throughput, batch and customization are structural), and it is orthogonal to all
four defects. CloudWatch reads move from per-ModelId enumeration to the four
undimensioned aggregates — verified equivalent over 2026-09-14 to 09-24, agreeing
to four decimal places, the aggregate very slightly larger because `list_metrics`
returns only recently-active series.

### Accepted limitation

Ceiling pricing over-estimates for models much cheaper than the priciest. The
cheapest here are two orders of magnitude below it, and two models currently bill
nothing for cache-write, so the factor is unbounded. A large embedding or
small-model batch job can trip the cap at a small fraction of intended spend.
Accepted deliberately for simplicity; stated in the README. The remedy if it
bites is an exact-match `{ModelId: rate}` override defaulting to the ceiling —
equality only, never substring or normalisation, so it cannot reopen this class.

## Figures

Machine-local policy bars spend totals, unit costs, budgets, cap thresholds and
bill figures from the tracker, because the tickets branch auto-pushes to the
public GitHub mirror. Ceiling constants, threshold, observed rates, back-test
distribution and incident figures are in the operator's local-only note
`~/Desktop/bedrock-cap-redesign-local-only/design.md`. Implement from that file;
copy no figure into this ticket, a comment, a session log, a commit or the README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_refresh_rates`, `_rate_for`, `_seed_for`, `_normalise`,
  `_strip_billing_region`, `_marketplace_rate_key`, `_rate_key_for_ce_group`,
  `SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`, `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKENS_PER_RATE_UNIT` and the `TOKEN_METRICS` multipliers are gone
  from the module. Checked: a test asserting none of those names survives.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` issues exactly four undimensioned `GetMetricData` queries
  per region and calls no `list_metrics` on the enforcement path. Checked: a test
  asserting the stubbed client recorded four queries per region and zero
  `list_metrics` calls.
- [ ] A `CEILING` mapping gives one rate per token metric, each at least the
  highest rate for that direction in the recorded CE payload. Checked: a test
  deriving observed rates from the fixture and comparing.
- [ ] Enforcement compares `max(ceiling_estimate, ce_spend)` against the
  threshold, and `_ce_spend_today` classifies by predicate (service equals
  `Amazon Bedrock` or ends with the Bedrock Edition suffix), not an allowlist.
  Checked: a test proving the predicate matches every Bedrock service in the
  fixture, including the five the allowlist omitted.
- [ ] The cap does not release on a tick where every CloudWatch query returned no
  datapoints. Checked: a test asserting the deny stays attached on an empty read.
- [ ] Threshold and warning values in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` match
  the design note. Checked: `terraform plan` shows only those env changes.
- [ ] `state["rates"]`, `state["rates_day"]`, `metered_estimated`, `MeteredRate`
  and the `" (estimated)"` rendering are removed. Checked: a test asserting the
  persisted state document carries no rate table.
- [ ] A daily guard compares the ceiling estimate for a settled day against CE for
  that day and raises an SNS warning when the estimate is below actual; it cannot
  attach or detach the policy. Checked: a test driving an invariant violation and
  asserting a warning with no IAM call.
- [ ] A daily `list_metrics` ModelId diff warns on a ModelId outside the recorded
  known set. Checked: a test adding an unknown ModelId to the fixture.
- [ ] Per-model token counts are logged on the warn and trip paths only, with no
  prices and no matching. Checked: a test asserting the log line on trip and its
  absence on a normal tick.
- [ ] Tests run off recorded real CE and `list_metrics` payloads committed to the
  repo, the CE one containing CamelCase, snake_case, `_Global` and a non-token
  usage type. Checked: a property test asserting every ModelId in the recorded
  `list_metrics` is priced by the ceiling with no fallback path.
- [ ] The README states the accepted over-estimate, the effective-cap band
  qualitatively, and that the figure is an upper bound, not an estimate of actual
  spend. Checked: reading the rendered section.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`
  proves every acceptance criterion above that names a test.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `make typecheck` are the commit gate.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify` before push, per AGENTS.md.
- `python3 scripts/terraform_prod.py plan --out <scratch>/plan.tfplan` must show
  only the intended Lambda env and code changes before any apply.

## Out of scope

SSM write concurrency and the `signal_unavailable` release deadlock: fourteen days
of logs show zero occurrences of either, against roughly seven thousand pricing
failures.
